problem: Evaluate offline RL on datasets that reflect narrow coverage, human/non-Markovian behavior, suboptimal mixtures, sparse rewards and undirected data rather than only online-RL replay.
contribution: D4RL provides heterogeneous fixed datasets, simulator-based evaluation and a normalization/tuning protocol that exposes failures hidden by simple policy-generated data.
algorithm: A benchmark rather than one learning algorithm: construct tasks/data with specified collection processes, separate tuning and final tasks, train offline methods and normalize returns to random/domain-expert references.
observations: Domain-dependent state observations or image inputs; CARLA uses48×48first-person RGB and is partially observable. Some collection policies have hidden waypoint memory not represented in learner observations.
actions: Task-specific continuous controls across navigation, dexterous manipulation, kitchen interaction, locomotion and simulated driving.
embodiment_and_data: Typically roughly1M fixed transitions per task, with different datasets sharing simulators. Maze2D/AntMaze planner-generated data, human demonstrations, cloned/expert mixtures, Flow and CARLA controller data are intentionally heterogeneous.
experiments: Compare offline learners across dataset types and hold out evaluation tasks from hyperparameter tuning. Analysis finds stitching/mixture/human-limited data remain difficult even when conventional RL replay looks successful.
baselines: BC, online/offline SAC, BEAR, BRAC, AWR, BCQ, cREM and AlgaeDICE; CQL appears in discussion of conservative methods. Online SAC has different data-collection access and is a contextual reference.

quantitative_result.value: NOT_EXTRACTED: individual algorithm/task table scores were not transcribed. Normalization is100×(return−random_reference)/(expert_reference−random_reference), so0/100are reference returns, not universal failure/success percentages; random reference averages100episodes.
quantitative_result.location: PDF p7 Evaluation protocol, p8 benchmark discussion

limitations: Mostly simulated robotics/driving/traffic, not standardized physical evaluation. Extensive online hyperparameter tuning can overstate offline deployment performance. Expert references differ by domain, and dataset coverage/collection policies strongly affect outcomes.
code_and_license: Paper says benchmark/data are released; this review verifies primary fulltext but does not establish current package, dataset-asset licenses or executable compatibility.
hardware_adaptation: Reuse the discipline of explicit collection-process metadata, development/final splits and mixed-quality data stress tests. Never display D4RL normalized returns as Explorer physical success rates; use measured task-specific rewards and observation contracts.
